author: Jim Lowe Staff Writer
title: VSO Holiday Pops celebrates!: Storytelling, from 'A Christmas Carol' to new Jewish fable | Rutland Reader | rutlandherald.com
text:
The Vermont Symphony Orchestra Holiday Pops includes all the usual seasonal musical favorites, but it takes a new and unique look at Charles Dickens’ beloved “A Christmas Carol.”
“I’m trying to make it sort of like a movie in that there’s musical underpinning that goes well with the story,” says VSO Music Director Andrew Crust who is conducting.
“I’ve added a few sound effects, which will add to the reading, such as when he’s talking about the church bells tolling, we’ve got bells tolling. When the specter enters the room, you’ll hear some sort of spectral scary sound effects from the percussion.”
The Vermont Symphony Orchestra will present its annual VSO Holiday Pops concerts Dec. 5-7: at 7:30 p.m. Friday, Dec. 5, at the Barre Opera House; 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Dec. 6, at The Flynn in Burlington; and 3 p.m. Sunday, Dec. 7, at Rutland’s Paramount Theatre.
The program features narrators M.T. Anderson and Marty Fogel, a world premiere of a new Jewish holiday story by Michael Schachter, plus young singers from the Youth Opera Program of Opera Company of Middlebury, including soprano Uliana Alehkin. And, of course, plenty of holiday carols, including the traditional carol sing-along — but with a twist.
Selections of “A Christmas Carol” will be read by award-winning Vermont author M.T. Anderson accompanied by music from Vaughan Williams and Prokofiev to film composer Howard Blake.
“I actually did something similar during COVID in Vancouver when, of course, the reader couldn’t even be in the same room,” Crust said. “So I did another abridged version of the Dickens, taking it down even further now, and added even more music.
“So it’s just a little microcosm of this story with musical backing.”
Anderson will appear in period clothing, and he’s going to read it in “a period way.”
“He’s really excited about it because, obviously as a writer, he really likes Dickens,” Crust said. “So it’ll be a little bit theatrical, a little bit cinematic in a way, with that musical underpinning.”
Among the five pieces within the Dickens segment, one is by Canadian composer Kelly-Marie Murphy.
“Her ‘Huron Carol Interlude’ is a really haunting, beautiful string orchestra piece, which is based on an Indigenous song and an Indigenous story from Canada, which is related to the wintertime,” Crust said.
In another segment, Blake’s “Walking in the Air” from “The Snowman,” a 1982 British animated television film, will be sung by Uliana Alehkin.
“She recently moved here from Russia,” Crust said. “I don’t remember her age, but she’s under 10 years old, and a really great singer who has been working with the Opera Company of Middlebury.”
All the young singers from Opera Company of Middlebury will be featured in the John Rutter arrangement of “The Twelve Days of Christmas” — with an Andrew Crust twist.
“I’ve adapted it to be Vermont-related,” Crust said. “I’ve changed all of the, you know, ‘Partridge in a Pear Tree’ and ‘Golden Rings’ and all of that, to Vermont-specific lyrics and they’re going to have props, and choreography. So that should be a lot of fun.”
And those young singers will be leading the Christmas carol sing-along.
“So that’s going to add a lot to the performance,” Crust said.
As the Christmas season has become more than purely a Christian time of celebration, the VSO commissioned “The First Snow of Chelm” from Michael Schacter, which will be narrated by Vermont jazz musician Marty Fogel.
“It’s not just a Christmas celebration,” Crust said of VSO Holiday Pops.
“I wanted people to learn a little bit about Jewish culture,” he said. “I asked Michael to find a folk tale or to find some history or maybe a Jewish authors’ short writing and create a work around that, which would be narrated with the music underneath like (Aaron Copland’s) ‘Lincoln Portrait.’
“And so that’s what he’s done with his story of a Polish town,” Crust said. “It’s a humorous funny story, but it also teaches you about how rabbis interact with the community and a little bit of Jewish history.
“And I really think it has a chance of being performed by other orchestras, hopefully around the world.”
“The Nutcracker,” as Crust says, never gets old, so the VSO will perform selections from Tchaikovsky’s classic ballet suite.
“I really wish we could find a way to do a production with dancers at some point, but it’s just incredibly complicated,” Crust said. “It’s a perennial classic with wonderful music which I think doesn’t even really need dancers.”
And there’s much more, from Samuel Coleridge-Taylor’s to Leroy Anderson’s “Sleigh Ride,” likely something for everyone.
Crust is the first VSO music director to conduct the annual VSO Holiday Pops concerts in more than three decades.
“It’s important because there’s a lot of folks who come only for this, so this is maybe their first entry point into the orchestra world — and hopefully we can bring them in for something else,” Crust said. “So, I do take it very seriously. For a lot of people, it’s their yearly tradition — so we’re happy to do it.”
